language.script: Varies by region — Devanagari (north), Dravidian scripts (south)
language.script_notes: Hindi/Devanagari script dominates the north; the four major Dravidian scripts (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam) dominate the south — each visually distinct and a strong regional tell. English appears widely alongside local scripts nationwide.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Inconsistent nationally; several bollard designs documented without one dominant standard.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Simple steel guardrail on major highways; often minimal or absent on rural/local roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow outside/white inside, white outside/white inside, and yellow outside/yellow inside all seen depending on road type and state.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal formal curbing outside major cities; extremely dense, chaotic mixed traffic (pedestrians, animals, rickshaws, vehicles sharing the same space) is itself a strong national tell.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The single most reliable India-specific tell is the Street View imagery itself: much of India's coverage comes from an unofficial, low-quality third-party camera that renders everything with a distinctive soft, slightly 'foggy' look unlike Google's own Gen 2-4 cameras.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs are the default on most urban/suburban construction nationwide (used as usable rooftop space); temple architecture diverges sharply by region — see North/South profiles.
architecture.roof_material: Flat poured concrete overwhelmingly dominant nationwide, a strong general India/South Asia tell versus pitched-roof-dominant countries.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete-frame construction with brick infill is standard in cities; painted or exposed brick/concrete-block low-rise buildings; ornate temple architecture (Nagara-style in the north, Dravidian-style in the south) is the most visually distinctive built element nationwide.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Often unpainted grey concrete or a mix of bright, varied paint colours on shopfronts and houses; densely layered with overhead wiring and signage.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Flat-roofed multi-story concrete buildings with rooftop water tanks; Hindu temples (Nagara shikhara towers in the north, Dravidian gopuram gateway towers in the south); dense, colourful market streets.

nature.vegetation: Extremely varied by region — the fertile Indo-Gangetic Plain and Thar Desert in the north/northwest, lush tropical Western Ghats forest and coastal palm groves in the south, distinct Southeast Asian-influenced hill/forest terrain in the northeast. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: The Himalayas form the northern border; the vast Indo-Gangetic Plain dominates the north; the Deccan Plateau and Western/Eastern Ghats define the south; a long coastline on both the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.
nature.climate_signature: Overwhelmingly varied by region and monsoon season — hazy and dusty in the north's dry season, lush and green in the south and during monsoon.

vehicles.plate_color: White with black text for private vehicles, yellow with black text for commercial vehicles, black with yellow text for self-drive rentals, green for electric vehicles.
vehicles.plate_format: Two-letter state code + two-digit RTO code + up to two series letters + four-digit number (e.g. 'DL 01 AB 1234'); a small 'IND' text with an Ashoka Chakra emblem appears on newer plates.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Auto rickshaws ('tuk-tuks', commonly green-and-yellow) are a near-universal, unmistakable India/South Asia tell; Maruti Suzuki, Tata and Mahindra dominate the car market; extremely dense, mixed traffic including bicycles, motorbikes, and sometimes animals sharing the road.

google_coverage.camera_generation: A mix of standard Google Gen 2-4 coverage in major cities and a distinctive unofficial third-party camera elsewhere, which produces noticeably lower-quality, softer/'foggy' imagery unlike anywhere else in the world.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring where official coverage exists; the unofficial camera imagery has its own distinct visual signature.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Coverage concentrated in and around major cities; the unofficial camera's distinctive look is itself one of the most reliable ways to identify India at a glance.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Indo-Gangetic Plain geography and vegetation in border regions, similar dense traffic and architecture in parts of North India
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Pakistan and Bangladesh use Urdu (Perso-Arabic script) and Bengali (its own script) respectively, both visually distinct from India's Devanagari/Dravidian scripts; India's plate format and auto-rickshaw colour schemes also differ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares Devanagari script and Hindi-adjacent language roots, similar Himalayan foothill terrain in the north
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Nepal's plates and flag/signage differ from India's; Nepal drives on the left as India does, so terrain and specific temple architecture (more Newari/Nepali pagoda-style) are the more reliable separator in border regions.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Dravidian-adjacent (Tamil) language presence in the south, similar tropical coastal palm vegetation
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Sri Lanka uses Sinhala script predominantly alongside Tamil, distinct from South India's Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam-only signage; Sri Lanka is an island with no land border, so context alone often resolves it.
